title: Restart-while-working breaks things: 4 verified mechanisms + graceful-restart design
summary: User-observed and code-verified: restarting the daemon while workers/loops are active breaks in-flight work via 4 mechanisms. (1) NO CLIENT RETRY — lib/mcp-core.js makeCall resolves {error: daemon unreachable} on the FIRST connection error; workers mid-tool-call during the restart window get hard failures (a mandatory-consult bench arm fails or silently proceeds cold → contaminated results; a worker mid-complete_task loses its report). (2) BLIND DEMOTION — daemon.js:112 demotes every running agent to unknown on boot; the staleness sweep then releases their claims, so a worker whose OS process survived the restart can have its task RE-CLAIMED by the heartbeat → duplicate/colliding work (likely behind mid-task kills/double-spawns observed this session). (3) WORKSPACE DEFAULT RESET — on boot the global workspace re-pins to whichever session hook fires next (caused the wrong-overlay embedding backfill); mostly defanged by per-request workspace (#6 writes, #15 reads) but the boot window still rides the global default. (4) NO SAFETY SURFACE — no /quiesce, /drain, or /version; activation was verified by hand-grepping targetOverlay counts. FIX DESIGN: (a) hooks/restart-daemon.sh — check list_agents/loops, warn/drain if active, restart, verify new /version (git HEAD) endpoint matches disk, never touch the workspace pin; (b) bounded retry in makeCall on ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET (~3x500ms) so brief restarts are invisible; (c) stop blind-demoting on boot — keep the agent registry and let the existing staleness sweep (real liveness windows) decide, so surviving workers keep claims.
